name: The Nation cryptic crossword No 3433
preamble: Puzzled? No more cross words! Read Kosman and Picciotto on “Solving The Nation’s Cryptic Puzzles.” Or watch this video.

clue.text: Jokester in Alabama is a religious figure

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means the first is placed inside the second

blocks.note: a card is a comic, a joker
taken as written
AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama

explanation.surface: A comedian from the Deep South turns out to be a figure of religious standing.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'in' does double duty in the surface but here is simply read as written: CARD, then IN, then AL.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal is a senior Catholic prelate, so a religious figure; the Arizona Cardinals are one of the grid's football teams.

clue.text: Ranch hand is shy, taking bow awkwardly

indicators.note: done awkwardly, the letters come out clumsily rearranged
a word taking something in holds it inside itself

blocks.note: coy means bashful, shy
the letters of bow, jumbled

explanation.surface: A bashful ranch worker makes a clumsy bow.
explanation.walkthrough: COY is split by the jumbled bow: CO-WBO-Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy is a man who herds cattle on a ranch, a ranch hand; the Dallas Cowboys are a football team.

clue.text: Steal ring, and twitch like a machine

blocks.note: to rob is to steal
a ring is round like the letter O
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A thief nicks a ring and twitches mechanically.
explanation.definitionFit: Robotic describes stiff, mechanical movement, the way an automaton or machine behaves.

clue.text: Entangle ex-president and father, having left the czar's seasonal residence

indicators.note: things that have left a place are no longer in it, so these letters go

blocks.note: W is George W. Bush's nickname
pa is an informal word for father
the Winter Palace in St Petersburg was the czars' winter home

explanation.surface: Tangling up an old president and a dad as they walk out of the Russian royal palace.
explanation.walkthrough: Take W (Bush's nickname) and PA out of WINTER PALACE and INTERLACE remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To interlace is to weave strands together so they cross, which is to entangle them.

clue.text: Televise advertisement for ventilation seal

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
a plug is a piece of promotion

explanation.surface: Putting an advert on TV for an air-conditioning gasket.
explanation.definitionFit: An air plug is a stopper fitted to an air vent or duct, closing off the ventilation.

clue.text: One visited a writer, mid-morning, after all-night party

indicators.note: the middle of a word keeps only its central letter
coming after the party means the morning piece is placed second

blocks.note: a rave is an all-night dance party
the central letter of morning

explanation.surface: Someone dropped in on an author mid-morning, still buzzing from an all-night party.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer is Edgar Allan Poe, whose poem The Raven has the bird visit the narrator. The Baltimore Ravens are a football team.
explanation.definitionFit: In Poe's poem, a raven taps at the narrator's chamber door and comes in, so it is the visitor.

clue.text: Bump into black aircraft engine

blocks.note: to ram something is to bump hard into it
jet is a deep glossy black

explanation.surface: Colliding with a dark jet engine.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs on into the light at 28, which says only 'See 5'. Both halves are themed NFL team names.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramjet is a type of jet engine that compresses air by the plane's forward speed alone.

clue.text: Backlog: It reveals, in part, a Hitchcock classic

indicators.note: read back, the run of letters goes from right to left
only part of the phrase is used, a run of consecutive letters inside it

blocks.note: a run of letters from the end of the first word through the start of the last

explanation.surface: Reading through a backlog, one finds a classic Hitchcock film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backlog' looks like a single word, but its first half is the reversal signal and its second half starts the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo (1958), starring James Stewart, is one of Alfred Hitchcock's most celebrated films.

clue.text: What you might find on a shirt or sweater: "Wanna make out?"

definitions.text: What you might find on a shirt or sweater

blocks.clueFragment: What you might find on a shirt or sweater
blocks.note: first meaning: the edge of a garment around the throat
second meaning, read cryptically: a chat-up line asking someone to neck

explanation.walkthrough: To neck is slang for to kiss and cuddle, so a line inviting that is a neck line.
explanation.definitionFit: A neckline is the opening of a garment at the throat; split in two it becomes a pickup line about necking.

clue.text: Like some plumbing Rodin sculpted while eating a donut

indicators.note: sculpted material is reshaped, so the letters are worked into a new form
something eating takes food inside itself, so the other piece goes within

blocks.note: the sculptor's name, used as letters
a donut is ring-shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Rodin carves a statue while snacking on a donut.
explanation.walkthrough: Rodin was famously a sculptor, which makes 'sculpted' read as a description rather than an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Indoor plumbing is plumbing inside the house, as opposed to an outhouse, so indoor describes it.

clue.text: Horse opera mostly captivating above-average word maven

indicators.note: most of something, but not all, means its last letter is dropped
to captivate is to hold captive, so this one encloses the other

blocks.note: horse opera is slang for a western film
a B is an above-average school grade

explanation.surface: A cowboy film that wins over a better-than-average lexicographer.
explanation.walkthrough: Noah Webster compiled the first great American dictionary; his name became a byword for a word expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Webster, the American lexicographer, is the archetypal authority on words, a word maven.

clue.text: Digital crime running rampant after UN's about-face

indicators.note: an about-face turns to point the other way, so the letters run backwards
running wild leaves the letters in disorder
coming after the organisation's piece, the crime piece is placed second

blocks.note: the United Nations' abbreviation, turned round
the letters of crime, scrambled

explanation.surface: Cybercrime runs wild after a United Nations policy U-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Digital data is expressed in numbers, so numeric is a synonym for digital.

clue.text: Less central skeptic is overheard skipping the introduction

indicators.note: skipping the introduction leaves out the opening letter
what is overheard is caught by ear, so the spoken form counts

blocks.note: a skeptic is a doubter; without its first letter it is said the same way as the answer

explanation.surface: A doubter is caught eavesdropping, having walked in after the opening remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: A skeptic is a DOUBTER; drop the D and OUBTER is pronounced exactly like OUTER, the silent B doing the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Outer means further from the middle, so it is the comparative idea of being less central.

clue.text: Pride participant starts to look into optional nudity

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their first letters

blocks.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A marcher at a Pride parade considers going naked, which is optional.
explanation.walkthrough: Pride suggests a gay pride march, but here it is a group of lions. The Detroit Lions are a football team.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of lions is called a pride, so a lion is a member of one.

clue.text: Clinton's legislative proposal

blocks.note: first meaning: the former US president's first name
second meaning: a draft law put before a legislature

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive makes it look like one proposal belonging to Clinton; the 's is read as 'is', joining two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Clinton was the 42nd president, and a bill is a draft law brought before Congress or Parliament.

clue.text: Burn leads to rule reversal for phone accessory

indicators.note: the word itself says the letters are to be turned back to front
something that leads to another comes first, before it

blocks.note: to char is to scorch or burn
reg is short for regulation, a rule

explanation.surface: A scorching leads to an about-turn in the rules about phone gadgets.
explanation.definitionFit: A charger is the lead and plug that refills a phone's battery; the Los Angeles Chargers are a football team.

clue.text: I run after ecstasy

indicators.note: coming after the drug's letter, the running piece is placed second

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
to go is to run, as a machine goes

explanation.surface: Someone goes jogging after taking a party drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the definition: the self.
explanation.definitionFit: The ego is the self, the 'I' of psychology, the part of the mind that says I.

clue.text: Source of sweat at Northern university

blocks.note: sweat runs from the brow, the forehead
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: Students perspire at a college up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northern university' looks like one phrase, but only the last word is the definition. The Cleveland Browns are a football team.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown University in Providence, Rhode Island, is one of the Ivy League colleges.

clue.text: Struggle with ghastly death burp

indicators.note: something ghastly is horribly mangled, so the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: nine letters taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Fighting against a horrible, deadly belch.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hard put to do something is to find it very difficult, so to struggle.

clue.text: Internet presentations raised worry about nasty scab

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word turns it upside down, so it reads upward
nasty treatment leaves the letters messed up and rearranged
to go about something is to surround it on both sides

blocks.note: to stew is to worry, and here it is turned upside down
the letters of scab, jumbled

explanation.surface: Fretting over a nasty scab that keeps getting worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Webcasts are broadcasts streamed over the internet, live presentations online.

clue.text: Snoopy, perhaps a little late, is a national symbol

indicators.note: arriving a little late misses the start, so the opening letter is lost

blocks.note: Snoopy in the Peanuts strip is a beagle; 'perhaps' marks an example

explanation.surface: Snoopy, running a bit behind, is somehow a symbol of the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The bald eagle is the US national bird. The Philadelphia Eagles are a football team.
explanation.definitionFit: The bald eagle is the emblem of the United States, appearing on its Great Seal.

clue.text: Hawn almost taking on Italian playwright

indicators.note: almost the whole name means it stops one letter short
a word taking something on holds it inside itself

blocks.note: Goldie Hawn is the American comic actress
taken as written

explanation.surface: Goldie Hawn nearly takes on the role of an Italian dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking on' reads as accepting a role, but it puts ON inside the shortened first name: GOLD-ON-I.
explanation.definitionFit: Carlo Goldoni was an 18th-century Venetian dramatist, author of The Servant of Two Masters.

clue.text: Hold pin erratically for ocean dweller

indicators.note: moving erratically, the letters follow no fixed order

blocks.note: seven letters taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Clumsily holding a pin for a creature of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolphin is a marine mammal that lives in the ocean; the Miami Dolphins are a football team.

clue.text: Poorly socialized boy, deprived of oxygen after weed bust

indicators.note: something bust is broken apart, so its letters are rearranged
oxygen is the chemical symbol O, so that letter is removed
coming after the weed piece, the boy piece is placed second

blocks.note: the letters of weed, jumbled
taken as written, before losing a letter

explanation.surface: A socially awkward lad, short of breath after a marijuana raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poorly socialized boy' looks like the whole definition, but the boy is wordplay; the definition is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Dweeby means like a dweeb, socially inept and nerdy, which is being poorly socialized.

clue.text: Sophia hiked fantastical land with one of the Medicis

indicators.note: in a down clue, hiked up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Sophia Loren is the Italian film star
Oz, the fantasy land of the Wizard of Oz, written upward

explanation.surface: Sophia Loren went hiking in a fairy-tale land with a Renaissance prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorenzo de' Medici, 'the Magnificent', ruled Florence and was the best known of the Medici family.

clue.text: Spider family found in bygone Philadelphia

indicators.note: found in means it sits inside the words that follow, a run of their letters

blocks.note: a run of letters across the end of bygone and the start of Philadelphia

explanation.surface: A clan of spiders discovered in old-time Philadelphia.
explanation.walkthrough: Nephila is a scientific name, the golden orb-weavers; the hiding place makes it fair even to a solver who has never met it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nephila is the genus of golden orb-weaving spiders, a group of related spiders, which the clue loosely calls a family.

clue.text: Follower of a fallen angel in subcontinental region

indicators.note: fallen things land in a heap, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: in the alphabet, b follows a
the letters of angel, rearranged

explanation.surface: A disciple of Lucifer is at large in a part of India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follower of a fallen angel' reads as a Satanist; the setter means the letter after A. The Cincinnati Bengals are a football team.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengal is a region of the Indian subcontinent, now divided between India and Bangladesh.

clue.text: Revolver returned in watertight lockbox

indicators.note: in means sitting inside the next words as a run of their letters
something returned goes back the way it came, so read right to left

blocks.note: a run of letters across the end of watertight and the start of lockbox

explanation.surface: A handgun handed back, kept in a sealed strongbox.
explanation.definitionFit: Colt is the maker of the famous six-shooter revolver; the Indianapolis Colts are a football team.

clue.text: Stand in front of barn with a piece of corn

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
in front of places that letter first, before the next piece

blocks.note: the first letter of barn
an ear is a cob, a piece of a corn plant

explanation.surface: A farm stand outside the barn sells corn.
explanation.walkthrough: In American usage an ear of corn is a single cob. The Chicago Bears are a football team.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to put up with it, as in 'I can't stand it', so bear means stand.

clue.text: Regret taking gym class in Indian capital

indicators.note: a word taking something holds it inside itself

blocks.note: to rue is to regret
PE is physical education, gym class

explanation.surface: Being sorry about having to do PE in New Delhi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian capital' points to a city, but capital here means money.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is India's currency, its money, which is a sense of capital.

clue.text: Cajolery from a ski instructor, maybe?

definitions.text: Cajolery from a ski instructor, maybe?

blocks.note: straight reading: flattery or persuasion meant to deceive
cryptic reading: a ski teacher's line of work happens on the white stuff

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: a ski instructor works on snow, so their job is literally one on snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A snow job is American slang for an elaborate effort to deceive or flatter someone, so cajolery.

clue.text: See 5
Taking a break from making a woolly surface?

blocks.note: first meaning: having a short sleep
second meaning: raising the fuzzy pile on cloth

explanation.walkthrough: Nap is also the raised fibres on cloth, and napping is the textile process of raising them.
explanation.definitionFit: Napping means dozing, a rest; in textiles it means brushing fabric to raise a soft fibrous pile.

clue.text: Leader of service is not a holy person

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of service
ain't is a colloquial contraction of is not

explanation.surface: The minister leading worship turns out to be less than holy.
explanation.walkthrough: The New Orleans Saints are a football team.
explanation.definitionFit: A saint is someone officially recognized as holy by the church.

clue.text: Unusual boot involved in autumn sport played by 15 inhabitants of the completed grid

definitions.text: sport played by 15 inhabitants of the completed grid

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement departs from the normal order of the letters
one thing involved in another is wrapped up inside it

blocks.note: fall is the American word for autumn
the letters of boot, rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange boot features in an autumn game.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifteen are NFL team names hidden in the grid as singular answers, from CARDINAL and RAVEN to RAM and JET.
explanation.definitionFit: American football is the sport of the NFL, whose teams' nicknames fill fifteen of the grid's answers.
